title: Generic-fibre specialization rectangles and chain lifting
statement:
Let $h:Y\to X$ be a regular morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes [def-exc-excellent-ring], meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres (the fibres remain regular after every finite extension of the residue field) [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Use geometric specializations and codimension after strict localization as in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex, def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Given a geometric specialization $\bar y'\rightsquigarrow\bar y$ above $\bar x'\rightsquigarrow\bar x$, there is a commutative square of geometric specializations
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\bar\eta'&\rightsquigarrow&\bar\eta\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ \bar y'&\rightsquigarrow&\bar y\end{array}$$
with the vertical arrows in the fibres over $\bar x'$ and $\bar x$ and with $\bar\eta',\bar\eta$ of codimension zero in those fibres. The top specialization has the codimension of $\bar x'\rightsquigarrow\bar x$. Any chosen finite saturated factorization of the base specialization lifts to a factorization of the top specialization with every intermediate point of codimension zero in its fibre and every lifted arrow of the same codimension as its base arrow. A saturated factorization has immediate arrows, with a codimension-zero transport allowed at the ends.

Put $c_h(y)=\dim\mathcal O_{Y_{h(y)},y}$, using local-ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The two vertical arrows have codimensions $c_h(y')$ and $c_h(y)$, respectively, and codimensions add along either path in the square. Thus, if the given bottom and base arrows have codimensions $b$ and $a$,
$$c_h(y')+b=a+c_h(y).$$
These assertions hold after the compatible strict localizations determined by the specified arrows; no assertion that an arbitrary global geometric fibre is connected is made.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemmas 4.3.2.3–4.3.2.6 (strict-local fibre integrality, lifting with preserved codimension, chains, and square); Expose XIV, Proposition 2.5.4 (codimension relation); additivity in excellent strict localizations.

mathlib_searches.query: A geometric specialization over a regular morphism of excellent schemes lifts to a commutative rectangle of generic points of fibres with codimension preserving saturated chains
Generic points of geometrically regular fibres lift geometric specializations uniquely after strict localization

For a flat morphism with geometrically regular fibres between excellent schemes geometric codimensions satisfy codim of specialization in source plus local fibre dimension at general point equals codim in base plus local fibre dimension at special point
